subject: Throughput sizing follow-up: FinEx performance targets and logs
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 10:14:00 -0400
Subject: Throughput sizing follow-up: FinEx performance targets and logs

Thanks for the call this morning — good conversation. Summary and next steps below so we have a concrete plan for sizing and a proposal we can iterate on.

Quick recap of what we heard from FinEx on the call:
- Primary use: real-time trade enrichment and short confirmation messages triggered on trade events (sub-200 token outputs typical, some longer explanations up to ~800 tokens for investigatory workflows)
- Latency SLOs: goal is P95 end-to-end generation <= 250ms for short confirmations; streaming per-token tail should be < 100ms when used
- Traffic profile: steady-state ~50 QPS (mostly small completions), peak bursts up to 200 QPS lasting 2–5 minutes several times an hour
- Concurrency: steady ~60 concurrent sessions, peak ~240 concurrent requests during burst windows
- Tokens/request: avg 120 tokens (input+output) on steady; peak requests can generate ~400 tokens when doing longer contexts

What we need from your side to finalize a sizing proposal:
1) Recent 48–72h request logs (timestamps, request size in tokens, response sizes, any streaming vs non-streaming flags). A CSV export or compressed logs are fine.
2) Confirmation on strictness of latency SLOs (is P95 250ms a hard requirement or a target we should optimize toward?)
3) Typical retry/backoff behavior and acceptable error budget during peak bursts (e.g., you can tolerate 1–2% transient errors during extreme bursts?)

What Redwood will do next:
- Take your logs and run a simulated throughput pass on our runtime to provide estimated tokens/sec, expected P95 latency, and recommended Dedicated capacity (GPU slab counts), plus a proposal with cost estimates.
- Provide options for smoothing bursts: autoscale vs buffering vs model variants.
- Include streaming tuning notes if you plan to use server-sent events / chunked responses for confirmations.

Attachments: finex-current-workload.csv (sample export), redwood-throughput-proposal.pdf (placeholder — will update after we analyze logs).

Next steps / asks:
- Alex: can you share the logs and confirm whether the 250ms P95 is a hard SLA?
- Marissa / Jonas: I’ll prep the sizing run once logs arrive; aiming to have a first-pass proposal within 48 business hours.

Thanks,
Rafael
Sr. Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@finex.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@finex.com
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 12:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing follow-up: FinEx performance targets and logs

Thanks Rafael — great summary. A few clarifications / answers inline: 

- Logs: I can export the last 72 hours and drop a sanitized CSV in the Drive link you shared. Will include a small sample of streaming vs non-streaming requests.
- Latency SLO: P95 <= 250ms is our target for confirmation messages (short outputs <= 64 tokens). For longer investigatory responses, we have a softer target: P95 <= 1s. So treat 250ms as high priority for short confirmations.
- Traffic profile: steady ~50 QPS matches our telemetry. Peak bursts are usually 1–5 minutes; rare peaks reach 300 QPS for <1 minute during market open on heavy days. Please size for sustained peak of 200 QPS and note that occasional 300 QPS spikes can occur.
- Tokens/request: average 120 tokens overall; short confirmations ~40 tokens. Investigatory flows up to ~800 tokens but those are low frequency (<1% of requests).
- Concurrency: steady ~60, typical peak ~250.
- Retries: we have simple exponential backoff; we accept up to 1% transient errors during extreme bursts but prefer graceful degradation (fallback to cached or simpler confirmation template) rather than outright failures.

I’ll upload the logs to the Drive folder by EOD. Naming: finex_telemetry_20260612.csv and sample_streaming.pcap (compressed).

Alex
Senior Platform Engineer
FinEx

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:20:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing follow-up: Throughput sizing follow-up: FinEx performance targets and logs

Appreciate the quick turnaround and clarifications — that helps a lot. A few notes after reading your reply: 

- Sizing approach: we’ll run two simulation passes on the logs you upload:
  * Steady-state pass (50 QPS, avg 120 tokens) to recommend a baseline Dedicated configuration that minimizes cost while meeting P95 targets.
  * Burst/peak pass (200 QPS sustained for 5 minutes, and a stress run for 300 QPS for 60s) to validate autoscale/burst capacity and check queueing behavior.

- Streaming: for short confirmations using streaming, our runtime can meet per-token latency < 100ms P95 with a small dedicated pool and aggressive prefetching. We’ll include a comparison of streaming vs non-streaming latency and cost.

- Batching and KV cache: if you have repeated prefixes (user-specific templates), we can dramatically reduce tokens/sec by leveraging prefix caching. Please annotate logs if you have such reuse patterns.

- Error budget: we’ll size with a 0.5% target transient error rate on steady-state and advise on graceful fallback strategies for burst windows to remain within your 1% acceptable error budget.

Action items / timeline:
- Alex: upload logs (as discussed).
- Rafael/Marissa/Jonas: we’ll run the simulation and send a first-pass sizing + cost estimate within 48 business hours of receiving logs. Expect a short write-up + spreadsheet and an optional follow-up call to review.

If acceptable, I’ll also open a HubSpot task and attach the plan so we have a single source of truth: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/3421

Thanks,
Rafael
